subject: Rstan 2.4.0 install script - automatic installation of packages

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Rstan 2.4.0 install script - automatic installation of packages
parts:
In another thread, an exceprt from the Rstan 2.4 install was script was posted, which includes:

install.packages(c("inline", "BH", "RcppEigen"))
+   install.packages("Rcpp", type = "source")

Why are those installed automatically instead of tested for? Moreover, for those of us who compile R and most packages from source, it looks as of our installs of inline etc. will be overwritten with binary versions.

Avi

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Rstan 2.4.0 install script - automatic installation of packages
parts:
On Friday, July 25, 2014 4:13:03 PM UTC-4, Avraham Adler wrote:
In another thread, an exceprt from the Rstan 2.4 install was script was posted, which includes:

install.packages(c("inline", "BH", "RcppEigen"))
+   install.packages("Rcpp", type = "source")

Why are those installed automatically instead of tested for? Moreover, for those of us who compile R and most packages from source, it looks as of our installs of inline etc. will be overwritten with binary versions.

It is possible to do. We just haven't done it yet. If the binary versions don't work, then there are deeper problems.

Ben

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: Rstan 2.4.0 install script - automatic installation of packages
parts:
I understand, and I'm sure that the binary versions will work, but those compiled from source are usually with optimizations which are lost when overwritten. For 2.3, I've had to reinstall `inline` after installing Rstan, and now for 2.4, it looks like I may have to reinstall more. Also, if the packages are already there, the install will be faster, no?

Avi

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Rstan 2.4.0 install script - automatic installation of packages
parts:
inline is a package with only R code.  As far as I know, there is no optimization level involved. 

RcppEigen and BH are packages mostly used for the c++ header files included, so I don't think optimization level would make a difference either.

Jiqiang
